## Current position

M4 has its four verification records, guard integration and cheap CI re-proof. The bounded transport-bound investigation closes scientifically unresolved ([both full-box pilots retain nonfinite physical enclosures after all final objectives run; independent graph, constraint and corrected-dual replay passes, with no finite physical candidate]{.claim}[C-297](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-297){.cid .st-preliminary}); certification remains pending. [OQ-42](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-42), [OQ-45](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-45) and [OQ-46](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-46) retain the stated limits. No failed proof or out-of-domain robustness box is relabelled as a pass. The guard artifact audit is [all four verified input boxes match the previous loaders; 48 of 48 retained pedestal states keep identical predictions and decisions; none of the 57 EC states is inside the exact proof boxes, so no EC certificate-based output check applies there]{.claim}[C-284](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-284){.cid .st-measured}.

The historical Tier A M5 prior study is retained ([all 256 retained Monte Carlo outputs are finite with zero native linear-step error codes, and 2048 sensitivity evaluations drop no rows; those codes do not establish nonlinear-residual or temporal convergence]{.claim}[C-292](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-292){.cid .st-measured}), while both audited finer ladders fail temporal convergence ([maximum paired changes remain 19.2654% and 1.9773% across the two refinements, exceeding the fixed 1% limit; all 99 retained rows are finite with zero native linear-step error codes and no exclusions]{.claim}[C-295](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-295){.cid .st-preliminary}, [the additional finer ladder has maximum paired changes of 1.7092% and 1.8560%, above the unchanged 1% criterion; all 99 assessed rows remain valid and no supported replacement step is established]{.claim}[C-296](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-296){.cid .st-preliminary}). The next audited ladder passes its first pair but fails the second ([the first pair stays below 1%, but the finer pair changes fusion power by up to 4.1372% and fails three quantities; all 99 assessed rows remain valid, so no replacement step is supported]{.claim}[C-298](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-298){.cid .st-preliminary}); no replacement step follows. The hybrid calibration passes the fixed pooled bar in both directions ([hybrid calibration covers 0.914/0.915/0.904 of the older hybrid test states; the reverse audit covers 0.887/0.869/0.900; all exceed the fixed 0.85 pooled bar]{.claim}[C-285](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-285){.cid .st-measured}). Every linearised uncertainty check remains nonlinear ([all four outputs fail the fixed 10% standard-deviation cross-check; disagreements are 46.2%, 43.4%, 43.1% and 59.7% for fusion power, thermal energy, central electron temperature and central ion temperature]{.claim}[C-287](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-287){.cid .st-measured}). A final refined propagation needs a supported step and a complete affordable design. Physicist sign-off and the physical-discrepancy limits remain open ([K-035](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-035)).

The completed diagnostics identify sustained fallback and internal branch mismatch ([the failing case rejects face seven on 24.766% of coarse and 82.539% of fine accepted states over (3,5] seconds; its median normalized global electron balance residual rises from 0.031813% to 0.962581%]{.claim}[C-299](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-299){.cid .st-measured}, [the failing case has different last-guess and accepted-state branches on 39.453% of coarse and 73.145% of fine steps over (3,5] seconds; during (3.5,4.5] seconds all fine accepted states fall back while 84.961% of last guesses select the surrogate]{.claim}[C-300](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-300){.cid .st-measured}), with a locally substantial but globally cancelling branch term ([the fine failing case has branch-term norm ratios of 0.723 for electron temperature and 0.982 for ion temperature; the signed global branch term cancels and the remaining coefficient lag carries the net defect]{.claim}[C-301](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-301){.cid .st-measured}). The [technical account](technical/uncertainty.qmd#internal-branch-diagnostic) states the limits and next checkpoint protocol. That protocol remains unimplemented and unsubmitted; no supported remedy follows.

## JOREK: finish J5, then decide its role {#jorek}

1. Done: the second case (b) job is analysed with the pre-registered window rule. n = 12, 16
   and 20 grow at the pedestal, weakly; n = 1–8 show no measurable growth by the end
   ([entry 73](log/73-case-b-n-scan-three-pedestal-modes.qmd)).
2. Done: the time-step check. Each of n = 12, 16 and 20 restarted from the same snapshot at
   Δt = 1 and Δt = 0.5; halving the step changes γ by about one part in ten thousand
   ([entry 75](log/75-time-step-check-of-the-case-b-pedestal-modes.qmd)). The doubled grid's
   axisymmetric state is ready.
3. Incomplete: the grid check ([OQ-43](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-43), the owner chose the full check). All listed chains have ended. The measured-cost projection invokes the existing stop rule; unused job slots do not permit continued links ([all three selected fine-grid checks remain incomplete; the measured-cost projection exceeds the existing compute envelope and further submissions stop]{.claim}[C-291](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-291){.cid .st-preliminary}).
4. Retain the unchanged-rule incomplete result and resource decision. Do not quote a fine-grid growth rate or infer stability from insufficient growth.
5. The owner then decides what JOREK becomes in the toolkit: a surrogate of a JOREK quantity,
   reference runs only, or neither. One case (b) n-scan costs about two six-hour node-jobs
   before any convergence check, which bears on that choice.

## M5 inputs and remaining gates {#m5}

[OQ-47](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-47) fixes the minimal Tier A scenario, priors and quantities of interest; [OQ-48](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-48) fixes the selected transport-discrepancy calibration. Do not reopen those decisions to repair numerical failures. Retain the same cases and physics through temporal refinement. Only a supported step and a complete affordable design permit final uncertainty and sensitivity propagation. Pedestal and equilibrium discrepancy remain unquantified; marginal conformal intervals do not supply a validated final-power error bound. Physicist sign-off remains the human gate.

## Complete the performance comparison {#performance}

Resolve the cancelled compute run, then agree a fresh bounded submission. Compare TGLF,
the final monotone surrogate and QLKNN using matched scenario, grid and solver settings.
Record compilation separately from execution, resource allocation, finite profiles, solver
status, profile errors and accepted-state guard rejection. Every output carries provenance.

Profile Newton separately to distinguish ensemble inference, transport/geometry work and
Jacobian construction. Keep unresolved overlap visible ([K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022)). Historical speed-up belongs
to the original model; timings from different hosts or drivers cannot establish final-model
speed-up.

**Done when:** a reproducible final-model runtime comparison and discrepancy report exist,
with allocation and solver settings stated.

Done 10 Oct. The cancellation matched a recurring node start-up failure

profile deviations [final v3 surrogate: T_e 7.7%, T_i 9.2%, n_e 11.4%, psi 0.32%; QLKNN: T_e 155%, T_i 128%, n_e 86%, psi 2.4%]{.claim}[C-159](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-159){.cid .st-measured} ([entry 35](log/35-matched-comparison-tglf-v3-qlknn.qmd)). The runner

## Train and integrate the response surrogates {#responses}

Define physically related case groups and label a small baseline. Keep entire groups together
in training and holdout sets. Inspect failed labels, sampled domains and physical integrals.
After the baseline, agree held-out accuracy metrics and targets with the owner.

Train structured EC ensembles and evaluate untouched holdouts. The selected pretrained
ITER pedestal is ported directly; no second network needs to learn its outputs. Integrate source and boundary
responses into TORAX behind guards with Tier A fallbacks. Supply channel adapters required
by the selected targets. Check gradients, finite execution, energy/particle balance, physical
rejection, fallback use and coupled cost. Pointwise profile errors alone do not establish
absorbed-power accuracy.

**Done when:** the reference datasets, checkpoints, accuracy results, guarded coupled checks
and matched cost measurements have provenance and meet the agreed criteria.

EC dataset v1 is labelled ([3120 of 3120 cases produce readable output (20 of 20 check cases); median 84.8 s of GENRAY time per case]{.claim}[C-164](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-164){.cid .st-measured}). The first baseline learns the totals but its
pointwise profile model does not beat the training mean ([driven current RMSE 3.30 kA/MW against 13.5 kA/MW for the training mean; pointwise profile model: current-density RMSE 2.20e4 A/m^2 against 2.09e4 A/m^2 for the mean]{.claim}[C-166](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-166){.cid .st-measured}), so the EC model
needs a structured profile output. [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) records that every case uses one equilibrium.
The owner then set the targets and restricted the states ([K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) option b); the structured
surrogate meets all three targets ([all three targets pass: absorbed power 0.01% and driven current 2.7% median relative error (targets 10%), heating centre 0.0036 median absolute error in rho (target 0.05)]{.claim}[C-168](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-168){.cid .st-measured},
[entry 38](log/38-structured-ec-surrogate.qmd)). Both the EC surrogate and the ITER pedestal
now run inside TORAX behind their guards ([runs under jit for both launchers with the surrogate serving the source; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-171](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-171){.cid .st-tested}, [runs under jit with EPEDNN setting the pedestal; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-173](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-173){.cid .st-tested},
[entry 39](log/39-ec-and-pedestal-surrogates-in-torax.qmd)).

## Close M3, then start M4 {#verification}

Audit the complete M3 criteria: held-out accuracy, differentiable guarded execution and
measured end-to-end speed-up. Transport accuracy alone does not close the RF/pedestal tasks.
Keep the ion-flux convention, monotonicity departure, default-root tolerance and domain limits
visible ([K-024](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-024), [K-025](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-025), [K-026](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-026)).

After M3 acceptance, agree verification properties and trajectory tolerances with the owner.
Prove properties over declared input boxes, calibrate uncertainty on held-out data, compare
trajectories against Tier A references and prepare per-surrogate verified-domain reports.
Certification review closes M4. Sampled monotonicity and raw ensemble spread are not
certificates.
